nodes.What it is: Feedback control measures the error between where a joint is and where it should be, and pushes in the direction that shrinks it. A PID controller does this with three terms: Proportional (push harder when far), Integral (fix a constant offset), Derivative (brake to avoid overshoot). Almost every motor in a robot runs some PID loop.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Pure code in simulation, instant visual feedback, and the SO-101 servos already expose P gains.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Mature; current practice is cascaded PID with feedforward and anti-windup, e.g. ros2_controllers PID controller exposes back-calculation anti-windup and feedforward, and PX4/Crazyflie multirotors run cascaded PID by default. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Universities (Caltech/Lund via Åström & Murray), ros2_control maintainers, PX4, Bitcraze
nodes.Best resources: Feedback Systems (Åström & Murray, free PDF); Modern Robotics ch. 11 videos; python-control library

nodes.What it is: To control something you first write down how it moves: equations that say how the state (positions, velocities) changes when you apply forces. State-space form, x_dot = A x + B u, is the common language used by LQR, MPC and simulators.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Mostly math and Python; needs some ODE comfort, which software students can learn quickly.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Model-based control relies on fast rigid-body dynamics libraries with analytic derivatives (Pinocchio) and physics engines (MuJoCo, Drake); 2026 work identifies object parameters with differentiable simulation (RigPI). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: MIT (Tedrake), Inria/LAAS (Pinocchio), Google DeepMind (MuJoCo), Toyota Research Institute (Drake)
nodes.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 2-3 (MIT); Feedback Systems ch. 2-3; python-control docs

nodes.What it is: Stability asks whether a controlled robot settles down or starts shaking and diverging. Engineers check it with eigenvalues, Bode plots (how the system reacts to fast vs slow signals) and Lyapunov functions (an 'energy' that always decreases). It explains why too-high gains make a robot oscillate.
nodes.Prerequisites: Dynamic system modeling & state-space; complex numbers
nodes._accessibility_reason: Abstract math with little visual payoff on its own, but tooling (python-control) makes plots easy.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Classical theory is settled; active work uses Lyapunov and sums-of-squares certificates to verify learned or nonlinear controllers. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: Feedback Systems ch. 5, 9-10; Underactuated Robotics ch. 9 (Lyapunov analysis); Modern Robotics 11.2

nodes.What it is: A controller needs a smooth target to follow, not a jump. Trajectory generation turns 'go from A to B' into a time-stamped path that respects speed, acceleration and jerk limits (trapezoidal or S-curve profiles). Smooth targets mean less shaking and less wear.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Library-driven (Ruckig) and directly visible on a real or simulated arm.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Online jerk-limited time-optimal generation is a solved, open-source problem for state-to-state motions (Ruckig, MIT licence); research moves to learned movement primitives (2025-2026 survey). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Ruckig (pantor), ros2_controllers joint_trajectory_controller, PX4 jerk-limited setpoints
nodes.Best resources: Ruckig README and examples; Modern Robotics ch. 9; ros2_controllers JointTrajectoryController docs

nodes.What it is: Each arm joint must follow its trajectory despite gravity and the pull of the other links. Simple PD control works at low speed; adding gravity compensation and 'computed torque' (using the arm's dynamic model to cancel its own inertia) gives precise fast motion.
nodes.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; Dynamic system modeling & state-space; forward kinematics
nodes._accessibility_reason: Fully doable in MuJoCo; on the SO-101 the servos are position-controlled, so torque-level methods stay in simulation.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Standard textbook material (Modern Robotics ch. 11, Murray-Li-Sastry ch. 4); research platforms like Franka FR3 expose 1 kHz torque control so students can run their own laws. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: Modern Robotics ch. 11 (computed torque); Coursera Modern Robotics Course 4; Pinocchio examples

nodes.What it is: Real motors have friction, backlash and delays that no datasheet lists. System identification means running test motions, recording data and fitting a model to it; tuning then picks controller gains that work on that model. It is how you close the gap between simulation and the real robot.
nodes.Prerequisites: Dynamic system modeling & state-space; least squares regression
nodes._accessibility_reason: Data fitting suits AI students; needs a real actuator to log, but an SO-101 or ODrive bench is enough.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Learned and hybrid models are mainstream: neural ODEs adapt mobile-robot dynamics online (AD-NODE, 2025) and VLM-seeded differentiable simulation identifies inertial/friction parameters (RigPI, 2026). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: ETH Zurich RSL, ODrive Robotics, research groups behind RigPI/AD-NODE
nodes.Best resources: python-control (system responses); ODrive controller tuning docs; Underactuated Robotics system-ID appendix

nodes.What it is: Instead of hand-tuning gains, you write down a cost (how bad errors and effort are) and let math find the best controller. The Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) does this for linear models in one function call, and is the classic way to balance a cart-pole or a drone.
nodes.Prerequisites: Dynamic system modeling & state-space; linear algebra
nodes._accessibility_reason: One library call (python-control, Drake) and a balancing demo in simulation within days.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: LQR remains the default stabilizer around equilibria and inside iLQR-style MPC; Tedrake calls it 'likely the most important and influential result' in optimal control. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 8 (LQR); Feedback Systems ch. 7; python-control lqr()

nodes.What it is: MPC repeatedly solves a small optimization: 'given my model, what are the best next N commands?', applies the first one, then re-plans a few milliseconds later. It handles limits (max torque, obstacles) directly, which is why legged robots, drones and cars use it.
nodes.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; basic numerical optimization
nodes._accessibility_reason: Solver tooling (acados, CasADi, do-mpc) is good, but formulating and debugging real-time MPC takes weeks.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Nonlinear MPC runs in real time with embedded solvers (acados, OCS2); 2026 work adds whole-body humanoid iLQR-MPC (arXiv 2611.04204), robust reduced-order MPC (CoRE-MPC) and GPU-accelerated robust adaptive MPC (A-SLS). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: acados team (Freiburg), ETH RSL (OCS2), CasADi team, do-mpc team
nodes.Best resources: acados docs and examples; CasADi docs; do-mpc tutorials; Underactuated Robotics trajectory optimization chapter
nodes.Sources:
https://docs.acados.org/
https://web.casadi.org/
https://www.do-mpc.com/en/latest/
https://github.com/leggedrobotics/ocs2
https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.04204
https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19250
https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20925

nodes.What it is: Trajectory optimization finds a whole motion at once, for example the best swing-up of a pendulum or a jump, by minimizing cost subject to physics. Methods include direct collocation (optimize states and controls at sample points) and DDP/iLQR (iteratively improve a trajectory with local LQR).
nodes.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; nonlinear optimization basics
nodes._accessibility_reason: Libraries exist (Crocoddyl, Drake), but convergence problems need maths maturity.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: DDP-family solvers (Crocoddyl FDDP) and direct methods in Drake are standard; contact-implicit and differentiable-contact trajectory optimization is an active 2026 research area. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 10; Crocoddyl examples; Drake tutorials

nodes.What it is: Impedance control makes a robot behave like a virtual spring and damper: push it and it yields, let go and it returns. Admittance control is the mirror image for stiff position-controlled robots: it measures force and turns it into motion. These are the control laws behind hand-guiding, safe contact and HRI (contact-rich manipulation tasks themselves are covered in the Manipulation branch).
nodes.Prerequisites: Joint-space control of robot arms; Feedback control & PID
nodes._accessibility_reason: Sim and ros2_controllers admittance controller are free, but real impedance needs torque-sensing arms (FR3) or a force sensor.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Mature on torque-controlled arms (FR3 joint torque sensors, 1 kHz); 2026 research learns stiffness and equilibrium point from demonstrations (Impedance Cloning) instead of raw trajectories. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Franka Robotics, ros2_control maintainers, DLR (robotics institute; not opened here)
nodes.Best resources: Modern Robotics 11.6-11.7; ros2_controllers admittance_controller docs; libfranka examples

nodes.What it is: Rather than commanding each joint, task-space control commands what matters: 'hand here, keep balance, don't hit joint limits'. Whole-body control stacks many such tasks and solves a quadratic program (QP) every millisecond to find torques that satisfy them all by priority. Humanoids and legged robots rely on it.
nodes.Prerequisites: Joint-space control of robot arms; Jacobians; quadratic programming
nodes._accessibility_reason: Needs dynamics, Jacobians and QP solvers together; doable in sim but steep for beginners.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: QP-based TSID-style controllers (TSID, ProxSuite, OSQP) coexist with learned whole-body policies; RSS 2025 accepted papers include several learned humanoid whole-body controllers (e.g. AMO, LangWBC). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: LAAS-CNRS (TSID), Inria Willow (ProxSuite), ETH RSL, UC San Diego (AMO)
nodes.Best resources: TSID repository and notebooks; ETH Robot Dynamics lecture; Pinocchio docs

nodes.What it is: An underactuated robot has fewer motors than ways it can move, like a cart balancing a pole, a ballbot or a walking robot. You must use the dynamics (falling, swinging) instead of fighting them: energy shaping to swing up, LQR to balance at the top.
nodes.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; Dynamic system modeling & state-space
nodes._accessibility_reason: Classic cart-pole/acrobot demos are free in sim and very visual; a real reaction-wheel or wheeled balancer is cheap.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Textbook problems are solved (MIT 6.832); 2026 work combines MPC and control barrier functions on real ballbots (Safe-Ballbot). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: Underactuated Robotics ch. 2-3 and lecture videos; MIT OCW 6.832; safe-control-gym cart-pole

nodes.What it is: A wheeled robot must follow a planned path while its wheels can only roll forward and turn. Controllers such as pure pursuit (aim at a point ahead on the path) and MPPI (sample many possible paths and pick the best) turn the path into wheel speed commands.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Nav2 controllers run out of the box in simulation; cheap differential-drive kits exist.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Nav2 ships Regulated Pure Pursuit and an MPPI controller as standard ROS 2 plugins; research adds learned adaptive dynamics (AD-NODE). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: Nav2 controller plugin READMEs; ros2_controllers wheeled-robot controllers; MPPI paper

nodes.What it is: A drone has no stable resting state in the air, so a fast control stack runs constantly: an inner loop holds the attitude rate, outer loops hold attitude, velocity and position. Learning it on a 29 g Crazyflie or in PX4 simulation shows cascaded control in action.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Crazyflie is small, open and safe indoors; PX4 SITL is free; tuning crashes are cheap at this size.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Cascaded PID remains the default (PX4, Crazyflie); Crazyflie also ships Mellinger, INDI, Brescianini and Lee controllers; RL end-to-end RPM control transferred after 18 s of laptop training (Learning to Fly in Seconds); 2026 nonlinear MPC planners for agile flight (NMPP). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: PX4 / Dronecode, Bitcraze, Caltech (Neural Lander), UZH/TU Delft groups (not opened)
nodes.Best resources: PX4 controller diagrams; Crazyflie controllers docs; Underactuated Robotics quadrotor section

nodes.What it is: Visual servoing closes the control loop through a camera: the robot moves until what it sees matches a target image or target object pose. It removes the need for perfect calibration because the error is measured directly in the image.
nodes.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; camera geometry basics; Joint-space control of robot arms
nodes._accessibility_reason: ViSP has tutorials and simulators; a webcam on an SO-101 is enough for a demo; matches the team's vision skills.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Classic IBVS/PBVS are packaged in ViSP (Inria); 2026 work replaces handcrafted features with pretrained visual geometry models for high-precision PBVS (VGM-VS). Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: ViSP tutorials and docs; Modern Robotics (kinematics); VGM-VS paper

nodes.What it is: Real robots are nonlinear and their parameters change (a payload, a worn motor). Nonlinear methods like feedback linearization use the full model; robust control guarantees behavior for a range of errors; adaptive control updates the model online while running.
nodes.Prerequisites: Stability & frequency-domain analysis; Optimal control & LQR
nodes._accessibility_reason: Heavy on proofs; payoff is real but takes months to master.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Learning-aware robust adaptive MPC on GPU (A-SLS, 2026) and learned-residual dynamics (Neural Lander) show the merge of adaptive control and ML. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Best resources: Murray-Li-Sastry book; Underactuated Robotics (partial feedback linearization); A-SLS paper

nodes.What it is: Instead of solving equations, sampling-based MPC simulates thousands of random command sequences in parallel on a GPU, scores them, and keeps a weighted best. It works even with contacts and non-smooth physics, and can make a simulated humanoid or quadruped move with no training.
nodes._accessibility_reason: Fits software/AI students: JAX or MuJoCo code, impressive sim demos, no hardware needed.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: MuJoCo MPC (predictive sampling, 2022), Hydrax (MPPI/CEM on JAX/MJX GPUs) and DIAL-MPC (diffusion-style annealing, full-order torque-level legged MPC; ICRA 2025 best-paper finalist per its repo) bring training-free whole-body control to sim and real quadrupeds. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Google DeepMind (MJPC), CMU LeCAR Lab (DIAL-MPC), Hydrax authors, Nav2 (MPPI)
nodes.Best resources: MuJoCo MPC repository; Hydrax README; DIAL-MPC paper and code

nodes.What it is: A safety filter sits between any controller (even a neural network) and the motors and minimally edits commands that would break a safety rule, like 'stay 20 cm from the wall'. Control barrier functions (CBFs) express those rules mathematically and are solved as a tiny QP every step.
nodes.Prerequisites: Optimal control & LQR; quadratic programming; Stability & frequency-domain analysis
nodes._accessibility_reason: Small QP code in sim is approachable; guarantees depend on a good model, which is the hard part.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: CBF-QPs are widely used (Ames et al. survey) and combined with MPC on real robots (Safe-Ballbot, 2026); safe learning surveys (Brunke et al.; 2024 survey) frame filters for learned policies; safety filters appear in RSS 2025 papers. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: Caltech (Ames), U. Toronto/TUM (Schoellig, safe-control-gym), Georgia Tech
nodes.Best resources: Ames et al. 'Control Barrier Functions: Theory and Applications'; safe-control-gym; Brunke et al. survey

nodes.What it is: Here machine learning improves or replaces parts of the controller: learning the dynamics model, learning a residual correction on top of a classic controller, or training a reinforcement-learning policy that outputs motor commands directly. The challenge is keeping it stable and safe on real hardware.
nodes.Prerequisites: Feedback control & PID; reinforcement learning basics; Model predictive control (MPC)
nodes._accessibility_reason: Matches the team's AI strength; residual RL on a classic controller is a safe entry point in sim.
nodes.Frontier state 2026: Residual RL (Johannink et al.), learned residual dynamics (Neural Lander) and fast sim-to-real RL for quadrotors (18 s training) are established; 2026 work learns impedance parameters (Impedance Cloning) and adaptive dynamics (AD-NODE). General robot-learning policies are covered in the Robot learning branch. Scope note: snapshot of the opened sources, not an exhaustive 2026 ranking.
nodes.Key players: U. Toronto/TUM (Schoellig), Caltech, Siemens/UC Berkeley (residual RL), MuJoCo community
nodes.Best resources: Brunke et al. safe-learning survey; safe-control-gym; Residual RL paper

robots_models.Name: Python Control Systems Library
robots_models.Key specs: Python module for analysis and design of feedback control systems (transfer functions, state space, Bode, LQR); BSD-3-Clause.
robots_models.Why it matters: The quickest way for Python developers to plot step responses and design PID/LQR controllers.

robots_models.Name: ros2_controllers
robots_models.Key specs: Generic ROS 2 controllers: PID (anti-windup, feedforward), joint trajectory, admittance, wheeled-robot controllers. Complements the ros2_control framework row from the Embedded branch.
robots_models.Why it matters: Gives real controller implementations the lab can run on SO-101 or simulated robots without writing them from scratch.

robots_models.Name: Ruckig
robots_models.Price / access: Community version MIT licence; separate Pro version
robots_models.Key specs: Online, jerk-limited, time-optimal trajectory generation for state-to-state motions.
robots_models.Why it matters: Makes any arm motion smooth and fast with one library call.

robots_models.Name: CasADi
robots_models.Key specs: Symbolic framework for numeric optimization and automatic differentiation; Python/C++/MATLAB.
robots_models.Why it matters: The standard way to write a custom MPC or trajectory-optimization problem in Python.

robots_models.Name: acados
robots_models.Price / access: Free, open source (licence file in repo, terms not checked)
robots_models.Key specs: Fast and embedded solvers for nonlinear optimal control; real-time NMPC; interfaces from Python/MATLAB.
robots_models.Why it matters: Takes an MPC from a laptop prototype to a real-time controller.

robots_models.Name: do-mpc
robots_models.Key specs: Python MPC toolbox (v5.1.2 docs): nonlinear and robust multi-stage MPC, moving horizon estimation.
robots_models.Why it matters: Beginner-friendly tutorials for a first MPC.

robots_models.Name: OSQP
robots_models.Key specs: Operator-splitting solver for convex quadratic programs; embeddable.
robots_models.Why it matters: The QP solver behind many CBF safety filters and linear MPCs.

robots_models.Name: ProxSuite
robots_models.Key specs: Proximal optimization toolbox (ProxQP) for QPs, C++ with Python bindings, aimed at robotics.
robots_models.Why it matters: Fast QPs for whole-body controllers.

robots_models.Name: Pinocchio
robots_models.Key specs: Fast rigid-body dynamics algorithms with analytical derivatives; URDF loading; Python bindings.
robots_models.Why it matters: Gives computed-torque, whole-body and trajectory-optimization code the robot's dynamics.

robots_models.Name: TSID
robots_models.Key specs: Task Space Inverse Dynamics: QP-based whole-body controller library built on Pinocchio.
robots_models.Why it matters: A ready reference implementation of humanoid-style whole-body control.

robots_models.Name: Crocoddyl
robots_models.Key specs: Optimal control library for robot control under contact; DDP/FDDP solvers.
robots_models.Why it matters: State-of-the-art trajectory optimization for legged and manipulation motions.

robots_models.Name: OCS2
robots_models.Key specs: Optimal Control for Switched Systems: SLQ/DDP-based MPC toolbox with ROS integration, used for legged and mobile manipulators.
robots_models.Why it matters: Industrial-grade MPC reference from a top legged-robotics lab.

robots_models.Name: Drake
robots_models.Key specs: C++/Python toolbox for model-based design and verification: multibody dynamics, LQR, trajectory optimization; used by MIT Underactuated Robotics.
robots_models.Why it matters: The tool behind the best free underactuated-robotics course.

robots_models.Name: MuJoCo MPC
robots_models.Key specs: Interactive real-time predictive control on MuJoCo: iLQG, gradient descent and predictive sampling planners.
robots_models.Why it matters: Shows a beginner MPC making humanoids and quadrupeds move in real time with no training.

robots_models.Name: Hydrax
robots_models.Key specs: Sampling-based MPC on GPU with JAX/MJX: predictive sampling, MPPI, CEM; online domain randomization.
robots_models.Why it matters: Python/JAX-native GPU MPC, close to AI students' tooling.

robots_models.Name: DIAL-MPC
robots_models.Price / access: Free code on GitHub (licence not checked)
robots_models.Key specs: Full-order torque-level sampling MPC with diffusion-style annealing; examples for Unitree Go2 and H1 in sim and real deployment.
robots_models.Why it matters: Training-free legged control that rivals RL in sim; a strong frontier demo.

robots_models.Name: PX4 Autopilot
robots_models.Key specs: Open autopilot with cascaded PID multicopter control, EKF2 estimation, SITL simulation, ROS 2 support.
robots_models.Why it matters: Industry-standard open drone control stack to study and modify.

robots_models.Name: Crazyflie 2.1+
robots_models.Price / access: Sold by Bitcraze; price not recorded from opened page (unknown)
robots_models.Key specs: 29 g open-source nano quadcopter; 7 min flight; 15 g max payload; 2.4 GHz radio and BLE; firmware with PID, Mellinger, INDI, Brescianini and Lee controllers.
robots_models.Why it matters: Safe indoor platform to write and test flight controllers.

robots_models.Name: ViSP
robots_models.Price / access: Free, GPL (commercial licence via Inria per site, not checked)
robots_models.Key specs: Open-source C++ Visual Servoing Platform: trackers, visual features, IBVS/PBVS control laws, simulators.
robots_models.Why it matters: Reference library to make a camera-driven arm demo.

robots_models.Name: Nav2 controller plugins (Regulated Pure Pursuit, MPPI)
robots_models.Key specs: ROS 2 path-tracking controller plugins: Regulated Pure Pursuit and Model Predictive Path Integral (MPPI).
robots_models.Why it matters: Production path-tracking controllers for any ROS 2 wheeled robot.

robots_models.Name: Franka Research 3
robots_models.Price / access: Commercial; price not on opened page (unknown, likely €5k+ band)
robots_models.Key specs: 7-DoF arm, 3 kg payload, 855 mm reach, joint torque sensors in every joint, 1 kHz low-level control via FCI/libfranka (Apache-2.0 client).
robots_models.Why it matters: Reference torque-controlled research arm; where impedance control is demonstrated in labs.

robots_models.Name: safe-control-gym
robots_models.Builder (if not in map): University of Toronto Dynamic Systems Lab / Learning Systems Lab
robots_models.Key specs: PyBullet cart-pole and quadrotor environments with constraints, for comparing control, learning and safety methods.
robots_models.Why it matters: Benchmark to compare LQR, MPC, RL and safety filters fairly.

top3.justification: Accessibility 5 and zero cost in simulation; directly improves the SO-101 stack the lab already uses and underpins every other control node. Visual impact is modest alone but strong once on a real arm or drone.

Training-free humanoid/quadruped demos in MuJoCo MPC, Hydrax and DIAL-MPC are very filmable, fit AI students' JAX/GPU skills and cost nothing in hardware; DIAL-MPC was an ICRA 2025 best-paper finalist per its repository.

A 29 g open Crazyflie (price unknown) lets students write and swap real flight controllers safely indoors; flight demos have high visual impact and connect to PX4/drone communities. Requires buying hardware and a positioning system, so cost is higher than pure sim.
